prompt: Assess this claim: Asian people have been denied voting rights because of race.

exact_response:
The claim is **true as a historical statement**, though the country and period matter.

In the United States, many Asian immigrants were barred from naturalization because of race. Because voting generally required citizenship, those restrictions also excluded them from voting. The Supreme Court upheld racial restrictions on naturalization in *Ozawa v. United States* (1922) and *United States v. Bhagat Singh Thind* (1923). Congress removed the remaining racial restrictions on naturalization in 1952.

Canada also explicitly excluded people of Chinese and Japanese ancestry from voting in certain jurisdictions, including people who were Canadian citizens.

This does not mean every Asian person was denied voting rights everywhere. A more precise claim is: **“People of Asian ancestry have historically been denied voting rights through racially discriminatory laws.”**
